phase_0.covers: On every push the authored UI source and its tests type-check under the authored policy (ui/tsconfig.tests.json covers ui/tests), and the unit tests run in Vitest under Bun with happy-dom. They hold these seams: the json-render Layout rejects on and watch and passes visible through; the wire helper omits an undefined optional and keeps null; RulesForm mounts with invalid data and shows the AJV errors; the SDK's resource MIME type is the one api/mcp-apps.json declares; PresentView refuses a chart specification that Vega-Lite's compile rejects, before any host call, with an alert that names the chart and no chart drawn; and the Apps bridge in ui/src/mcp-apps/main.tsx omits undefined optionals once, as a tool call leaves for the host, while PresentView passes its fields through. It does not prove that a valid chart beside a rejected one is still drawn (PresentView refuses the whole view, and no test holds either behaviour), rendering in a real host (the receipt gate mcp-apps-protocol-qualification) or any behaviour against a running server.

accepted_failures.decision: Docling stays the converter. Where a phrase changes font the library ends a text cell and joins cells with a space, so "(WRKFCNUSG)" is extracted as "( WRKFCNUSG )". Accepted for now; no newer version, option or pdfium changes it. An upstream report is drafted and is not filed yet.

phase_0.covers: A pass proves that every criterion pinned in qualification/docling/criteria.json passed, or is not applicable by design with the reason stated in the receipt, for the Docling crate Cargo.lock pins, called directly as a library on the clean commit the receipt cites: the model assets have the manifest's hashes and are the files the library loads; every fixture converts, is recognised as its declared format and holds the content SOURCES.json declares, a phrase set across a font change included, and a fixture without glyphs yields no invented text; each PDF and image fixture has one render per page that is not a flat colour unless the page is declared blank, and every text item, table and picture is located on a page with a box, by its own provenance or, for a PDF item the export leaves without one, by the one text-layer item with exactly its text; each PDF shows the library's placeholders for glyphs its fonts give no Unicode for on exactly the pages and in the numbers its fixture declares, which detects text that cannot be decoded and does not recover it; a truncated PDF is refused; a 1 ms budget is reported and changes the result; and a peak memory was read for every converter process. With accepted_with_limitations the same holds except for the criteria listed in accepted_failures, which fail. It does not prove that a box found through the text layer is the item's own (the receipt states the rule's two known wrong placements, and records each such item's distance to the item whose page was searched as a measurement with no threshold), a locator for DOCX items (the library gives none) or for XLSX and PPTX items (recorded without a rule and not pinned), the production ingest worker (locating through the text layer and detecting undecodable text are harness rules here; the construction gates ingest-locates-unlocated-items and ingest-flags-undecodable-text carry them into the product), a memory limit (peak memory is measured, never limited) or a conversion through the application.

A pass proves that every criterion pinned in qualification/mcp-apps/criteria.json was judged and passed on the clean commit the receipt cites: the App bundle built in the run is one HTML resource with the SDK's MIME type and a production React build; a fixture MCP server (the harness, answering from committed fixtures) lists and serves that resource, the four render tools and the app-only show and read_object over Streamable HTTP, with read_object declared by the product's schemas, served in ranged blocks that hash to the dataset's digest, and refusing an unknown digest or argument; and in the ext-apps basic-host example under Chromium each of the four views shows its own text with no alert and no serious or critical axe violation in the App frame, the present view drawing its chart and tables from the dataset it fetched. It does not prove the product server's show and read_object handlers or its blob store, rendering in claude.ai or ChatGPT (the acceptance gate mcp-apps-web-hosts) or the production MCP server over the Application.

phase_0.covers: Every CI run starts from a fresh clone of the pushed commit: bootstrap installs from the committed lockfiles only, builds the generator, generates, and builds and type-checks the UI before the gated steps run, so nothing can depend on an uncommitted file. Cargo's registry and target directory are restored from a cache keyed on rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock, with a fallback to the newest cargo cache of the same runner OS when none has that key, so `target` can come from another lockfile state and cargo's own fingerprints under `--locked` decide what is rebuilt; Bun's install cache is keyed on .bun-version and bun.lock and has no fallback. CI asserts that the checkout is unchanged directly after bootstrap (the deterministic-foundation gate) and not again after the gated steps, and it does not run the audit; `bun scripts/dev.mjs clean-checkout` asserts a clean tree after the whole sequence and runs the audit locally, and is a tool, not a gate.

construction.meaning: Kill and restart against the real RecordStore with JobHandler(&ClaimedJob); no duplicate effect; after restart leases are expired and pending jobs re-enqueued (`expire_leases`, `pending_jobs`); an attempt that dies without a restart is retried after its lease expires.

An item the converter leaves without a location (a PDF caption: the library drops its box) is located through the page text layer by the rule of qualification/docling/src/locate.rs: docling::pdf_text_layer_pages, the one text-layer item with exactly its text on the page of its parent or of its nearest located earlier sibling, with a box that has area and lies inside the page. An item the rule does not find is recorded as unlocated; it is never given a guessed box, and every location records which source gave it. The rule does not guarantee that the box it finds is the item's own: that file states the two known wrong placements (LOCATE_LIMITS), and the harness records each item's distance to the item whose page was searched without applying a threshold. Whether the product bounds that distance is the owner's decision, open until this gate is built

Text the PDF's fonts cannot map to Unicode is detected by the rule of qualification/docling/src/glyphs.rs (the library prints `/` and the glyph's name for each such glyph), is never indexed as words, and its page is reported as partly extracted. The detector has two known limits: it flags real text of the placeholder's shape that stands after a space (`/B747`, `/v100`, `/tmp123`), and it misses a placeholder glued to a preceding character (`x/g12`). A signal from the library that a glyph had no Unicode is preferred to this detector as soon as the library gives one
